thought.text: The readiness requires DB (migrations) + Redis. Let me understand what `docker compose up --scale app=0` will actually start for the local profile, since the app runs as a dev server (not container) but `provisioner`/`migrate`/`bootstrap` are in compose.yaml.

reasoning_content:
So `/health/ready` requires: database ready (goose migration + schema guard), redis available, permission cache, etc. Migrations must be applied. `env:up` does that for us.

Now let me think about the overall approach:

The `up` command:
1. `assertRuntimeEnv` — validate required env keys for the profile
2. `upLocalInfra` — `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.override.yaml [-f compose.monitoring.yaml] up -d --scale app=0`
3. `migrateLocalDatabase` — `pnpm nx run data:db:migrate` (goose migrations via docker exec postgres)
4. `bootstrapLocalAppUser` — `pnpm nx run data:db:bootstrap-app-user`
5. `checkLocalInstanceRegistryDrift` (up/update only)
6. `startLocalApp` — start `pnpm nx run sva-studio-react:serve` via local-dev-server-runner, wait for `/health/live` OK (60s)
7. `startLocalProvisioningWorker` — only for local-keycloak (not local-builder)

For `local-builder`, no provisioning worker. Good.

The compose `up` with `--scale app=0` — but app/provisioner have `image: ghcr.io/...`. With `--scale app=0`, the app service won't be created. But provisioner? The override adds `build: .` to app, provisioner, migrate, bootstrap. `--scale app=0` only scales app. provisioner would start with `build: .` → it would build the whole Docker image (takes a very long time, many minutes, huge). That's a problem.

Wait, let me re-check. `upLocalInfra` runs `docker compose ... up -d --scale app=0`. This starts ALL services in the compose project except scaling app to 0. So it would start: app(0), provisioner, migrate, bootstrap, redis, postgres, and monitoring services.

But `migrate` and `bootstrap` have `replicas`? No, only `candidate` has `replicas: 0`. So `migrate` and `bootstrap` are one-shot? They use `entrypoint: ./migrate-entrypoint.sh`. They're defined in compose.yaml without `profiles`, so they'd start on `up`. That would build the image (via override `build: .`) and run migrations... 

Hmm, this is getting complicated. Actually wait — let me reconsider. Do `migrate` and `bootstrap` run on `up`? They have `image: ghcr.io/smart-village-solutions/sva-studio` in compose.yaml, and override adds `build: .`. So on `up -d`, docker compose would start all of: provisioner, migrate, bootstrap, redis, postgres + monitoring. That's a lot, and building the image (Dockerfile build of the whole monorepo) would take a very long time and may fail.

Wait, but these one-shot jobs (migrate, bootstrap, provisioner, candidate) — do they have restart policies or profiles that keep them from running in a plain `up`? Let me look more carefully. In the production compose.yaml (for swarm), these are all part of the stack. But for LOCAL use, the `upLocalInfra` uses `compose.yaml` + `compose.override.yaml` (dev). Let me re-read: the local profiles use `getComposeArgs(env)` which is `compose.yaml` + `compose.override.yaml` (+ monitoring). So for local, it's using the SAME compose.yaml that's designed for the studio swarm stack, plus the dev override.

Hmm, that seems odd but let me check — maybe compose.yaml services other than redis/postgres are meant to be gated. Let me look again at whether migrate/bootstrap/provisioner have any local gating. Actually, they don't have `profiles`. So `docker compose up -d --scale app=0` WOULD try to start provisioner, migrate, bootstrap too.

Wait, that doesn't make sense for a local dev. Let me reconsider — maybe there's something. Let me look at the compose.yaml more carefully. Actually, this is the production compose used for the swarm stack. For local, the override file `compose.override.yaml` modifies app/provisioner/migrate/bootstrap to `build: .` and adds redis TLS + postgres ports.

So `up -d --scale app=0` would build the image once (shared across app/provisioner/migrate/bootstrap/candidate) and start provisioner, migrate, bootstrap. That's expensive and migrate/bootstrap are one-shot that would exit.

Hmm, wait. Actually this is concerning. Let me reconsider whether the local path really uses this compose.yaml. Let me re-read the code: `composeBaseArgs = ['compose', '-f', 'compose.yaml', '-f', 'compose.override.yaml']`. Yes, local uses compose.yaml + override.

But hold on — that would mean local `up` builds the production image and starts provisioner/migrate/bootstrap. That seems heavy. But maybe that IS the intended design: the local profiles reuse the exact same stack (app runs in dev server, but provisioner/migrate/bootstrap run as containers). Actually no — the dev server runs the app locally (pnpm nx run sva-studio-react:serve), not the container app. The container `app` is scaled to 0. So provisioner/migrate/bootstrap would still build the image and run.

This is a real concern for time. Building the Docker image (pnpm install + nx builds for ~9 packages + vite build) could take 10-30+ minutes and might hit memory limits (we have 7.6Gi RAM).

Let me step back and reconsider the scope of this task.

The task: "Install the assigned software and report the outcome based on objective evidence." The software is "SVA Studio". The installation guide is the runtime-profile runbook.

The realistic, self-contained installation path is:
1. Install toolchain (Node 24.15.0, pnpm 11.3.0) ✅ done
2. `pnpm install` ✅ done
3. `pnpm check:toolchain-consistency` ✅ passes
4. Set up local runtime config (base.vars / profile vars)
5. `pnpm env:up:local-builder` (or local-keycloak)
6. `pnpm env:smoke:local-builder` / `doctor` to verify

The challenge: `env:up` runs `docker compose up -d --scale app=0` which starts provisioner/migrate/bootstrap AND builds the image. That's very heavy.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider. Let me check if maybe there's a way the one-shot jobs are profiled. Let me look very carefully at compose.yaml for `profiles:` on any service. I grepped earlier for `profiles` and found nothing. Let me double check there's no profiles and whether migrate/bootstrap/provisioner would really start.

Actually, I realize I should reconsider the whole approach. The key question: is there a lighter, documented way to get the software "installed" and verified running?

Let me reconsider what "install" means here. This is a web application (SVA Studio). "Installing" it means getting it set up so it can run. The guide's canonical local path is `pnpm env:up:local-builder` or `pnpm env:up:local-keycloak`, then verify with smoke/doctor.

Given the constraints (7.6Gi RAM, no Keycloak available locally for local-keycloak, external mainserver not available), the most feasible is `local-builder`.

But the `up` command's `upLocalInfra` does a full docker compose up which builds the production image. Let me verify this is really what happens and whether it's feasible. Actually, maybe I'm wrong that it builds. Let me reconsider: the override file has `build: .` for app, provisioner, migrate, bootstrap, and `image:` for candidate. When you run `docker compose up`, services with a `build` section will be built if the image doesn't exist. The image name for `app` is not specified in override (it inherits `image: ghcr.io/...` from base? No — override replaces). Actually override sets `build: .` on app, but does it keep the `image: ghcr.io/...`? In compose, if you specify `build`, the image gets a generated name unless `image` is also set. The base compose.yaml sets `image: ghcr.io/smart-village-solutions/sva-studio` for app. Override adds `build: .`. When both `image` and `build` are present, compose builds the image and tags it with the `image` name. So `up` would build `ghcr.io/smart-village-solutions/sva-studio` from the Dockerfile.

That's a full build. Given the Dockerfile does `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` + builds ~10 packages + vite build, this is a big build. With 7.6Gi RAM it might OOM during vite/nitro build.

This is getting very heavy. Let me reconsider whether I should even go down the `docker compose up` path for infra, or whether there's a lighter way.

Actually — the essential infra for the app to run and pass health/smoke is just:
- Postgres (for IAM DB + migrations + app user)
- Redis (for session store)
- OTEL collector (for local smoke's `assertOtelLocal`) — but only if `SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING != 'false'`

The app itself runs as a local dev server (`pnpm nx run sva-studio-react:serve`), NOT in a container.

So the heavy parts of `docker compose up` are: app (scaled 0), provisioner, migrate, bootstrap, candidate (replicas 0), redis, postgres, + monitoring. Of these, provisioner/migrate/bootstrap would build the image and start. That's the expensive/unwanted part.

The cleanest approach given my constraints:
- Run the `env:up:local-builder` command as documented. But I'm worried about the image build.

Let me reconsider. Actually, maybe I'm overcomplicating. Let me just TRY `pnpm env:up:local-builder` and see what happens. But first I need the config vars in place, and it might take a long time to build the image.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the whole thing. Let me re-examine: is the image actually built during `up`? Let me reconsider whether `migrate` and `bootstrap` and `provisioner` are really started. Let me look at whether they have any guard. 

Actually, I realize the smarter and more robust approach given my environment:

1. Start ONLY the needed infra (postgres, redis, otel-collector) via docker compose directly (or let the env:up do it but be aware it may build image).

Hmm, but the guide says to use the canonical commands. Let me be pragmatic: I'll try the canonical `pnpm env:up:local-builder`. If the image build is the problem, I'll adapt.

But actually, let me reconsider the time budget. I have 600s per command. A full image build of this monorepo could exceed that. Let me first check: does the override actually cause a build, and are migrate/bootstrap/provisioner going to start?

Let me test by doing a `docker compose config` to see the resolved services, and check if there's `profiles`. Actually, the most reliable: let me just run `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.override.yaml config --services` to list services, and think about what `up --scale app=0` does.

Actually, I think the cleaner path, and one that avoids the massive image build, is:

Since the app runs as a local dev server and I only need postgres + redis (+ otel collector for smoke) as infra, I can:
1. Create the config vars files.
2. Manually start postgres, redis, otel-collector via `docker compose up -d postgres redis otel-collector` (subset). This avoids building the app image entirely.
3. Run migrations + bootstrap app user via the nx targets (data:db:migrate, data:db:bootstrap-app-user) with the right env.
4. Start the dev server.
5. Run smoke/doctor.

But this deviates from the canonical `env:up` command. However, the task says "You may perform actions that are reasonably necessary to carry out the installation" and "Treat the supplied installation guide as the primary source." The guide's commands are the primary path, but if a full image build is impractical, I should note it.

Hmm, let me reconsider. Actually, let me just first see what `docker compose config` reports and whether `up --scale app=0` would build. Let me be efficient and check the resolved compose.

Actually, let me reconsider even more fundamentally. Let me re-read `upLocalInfra`:
```js
run('docker', [...composeArgs, 'up', '-d', '--scale', 'app=0'], env);
```
where `composeArgs = getComposeArgs(env)` = `['compose', '-f', 'compose.yaml', '-f', 'compose.override.yaml']` or with monitoring.

So it's `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.override.yaml [-f compose.monitoring.yaml] up -d --scale app=0`.

This starts all non-app services. The `migrate`, `bootstrap`, `provisioner` services are in compose.yaml and NOT excluded by `--scale app=0`. So they WILL start, and since they have `build: .` (from override) or `image:`, they'd be built/run.

This is the crux. Building the production image is the expensive step. Let me estimate: the Dockerfile build runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (already have node_modules but Docker builds in isolated layer, so it reinstalls) + 9 nx package builds + vite build. This could take 15-40 min and risk OOM.

Given the 7.6Gi RAM and the risk, I think the pragmatic, still-faithful approach is to start only the required infra services (postgres, redis, otel-collector) rather than the whole production stack, because the app itself runs as a local dev server (not a container) in the local profile. The provisioner/migrate/bootstrap/candidate container services are not needed for the local dev server to run and pass health/smoke — their local equivalents are:
- migrate → `data:db:migrate` (goose) run locally
- bootstrap → `data:db:bootstrap-app-user` run locally
- provisioner → only for local-keycloak (Keycloak provisioning), not for local-builder

So for `local-builder`, the ONLY container infra needed is postgres, redis, and (for smoke) otel-collector. This is a faithful, minimal infra that matches what the local profile actually uses.

Wait, but the canonical `env:up` would build the image for provisioner/migrate/bootstrap even though their local equivalents run via nx. That seems like the compose.yaml is really the swarm/remote stack file being reused. Let me verify by checking if maybe there's a separate local compose. There's `compose.override.yaml` (dev) which is used for local. And the local dev-server runs the app locally.

OK here's my decision. I'll be pragmatic and evidence-based:

Plan:
1. Create `config/runtime/base.vars` with the required local dev defaults (this is the git-ignored canonical base, whose absence is a real gap in the repo for fresh clones — the guide treats it as canonical source #1). I'll populate it with sensible local dev values documented in the repo docs (postgres-setup.md, redis-setup.md, .env.example).
2. Create `config/runtime/local-builder.vars` (git-ignored) with the local-builder-specific non-secret values (SVA_MOCK_AUTH, VITE_MOCK_AUTH, VITE_PUBLIC_BUILDER_KEY, etc.). Actually, buildProfileEnv merges base + profile + local vars. The profile file is `config/runtime/local-builder.vars`. I need to provide the required keys. Since base.vars is the main carrier, I'll put most in base.vars and the builder-specific in local-builder.vars or local-builder.local.vars.

Actually, let me reconsider the env merging. `buildProfileEnv` reads:
- base.vars (config/runtime/base.vars)
- profile.vars (config/runtime/local-builder.vars)
- localOverride (config/runtime/local-builder.local.vars) — optional
- userQuantumEnv (~/.config/quantum/env)
- processEnv (overrides all)

So I can put everything in base.vars + local-builder.vars. For local-builder, the required keys (from PROFILE_DEFINITIONS):
COMMON_REQUIRED:
- SVA_RUNTIME_PROFILE (set by buildProfileEnv automatically)
- SVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
- IAM_PII_ACTIVE_KEY_ID
- IAM_PII_KEYRING_JSON
- ENCRYPTION_KEY
- SVA_MAINSERVER_GRAPHQL_URL
- SVA_MAINSERVER_OAUTH_TOKEN_URL
- SVA_MAINSERVER_CLIENT_ID
- SVA_MAINSERVER_CLIENT_SECRET
LOCAL_CONNECTION_REQUIRED:
- REDIS_URL
- IAM_DATABASE_URL
local-builder extra:
- SVA_MOCK_AUTH
- VITE_MOCK_AUTH
- VITE_PUBLIC_BUILDER_KEY

Plus for mock-auth profile, buildProfileEnv sets SVA_MOCK_AUTH/VITE_MOCK_AUTH/BUILDER_DEV_AUTH automatically via setMockAuthFlags. But assertRuntimeEnv still validates they're present — setMockAuthFlags sets them before validation? Let me check order. In buildProfileEnv: it sets SVA_RUNTIME_PROFILE, VITE_SVA_RUNTIME_PROFILE, then if mockAuth → setMockAuthFlags (sets SVA_MOCK_AUTH='true', VITE_MOCK_AUTH='true', BUILDER_DEV_AUTH='true'), then buildRuntimeAliases. So yes, SVA_MOCK_AUTH and VITE_MOCK_AUTH are set automatically for the mock profile. Good, so I don't strictly need them in vars, but I'll add for clarity.

VITE_PUBLIC_BUILDER_KEY: needs a value (any non-empty string). It's a Builder.io public key. For local mock, a placeholder value should be fine for the env validation (it's just required to be present and non-placeholder). But the Builder.io functionality would need a real key. For smoke, only /auth/login, /auth/me, /api/v1/iam/me/context, mainserver (skipped), otel, schema guard matter. So VITE_PUBLIC_BUILDER_KEY just needs a non-placeholder value. I'll set a local dev value.

Now for mainserver: local-builder requires SVA_MAINSERVER_* keys to be present (non-placeholder) for env validation. But the mainserver smoke is gated by `isMainserverCheckRequired` which for local profiles = `resolveRequiredFlag(env.SVA_MAINSERVER_REQUIRED, runtimeProfile !== 'studio')` = default TRUE for local (since profile != 'studio', fallback = true). So by default the mainserver smoke WOULD run and fail (no mainserver). I must set `SVA_MAINSERVER_REQUIRED=false` to make it optional (as the guide explicitly documents for the early test phase). But then the values SVA_MAINSERVER_GRAPHQL_URL etc. must still be present (non-placeholder) for env validation. I'll set them to localhost values (documented) so validation passes, and SVA_MAINSERVER_REQUIRED=false so smoke skips it.

Wait — but the required env validation requires SVA_MAINSERVER_GRAPHQL_URL etc. to be present. They just need non-placeholder values. I'll set them to local values like `http://127.0.0.1:3100/graphql` (won't be used since mainserver check is skipped). Actually the guide says mainserver URLs "bleiben trotzdem dokumentiert". I'll use plausible local values.

For OTEL: local smoke `assertOtelLocal` runs unless `SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING === 'false'`. It checks `http://127.0.0.1:13133/healthz`. If I run the monitoring compose (which includes otel-collector), then 13133 is up. Alternatively set `SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING=false` to skip both the monitoring compose AND the otel smoke check. 

But the guide's `up` for local uses `getComposeArgs(env)` = monitoring unless SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING=false. And the doctor/smoke otel check is skipped if SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING=false. To keep it simpler and avoid pulling the whole monitoring stack (prometheus, loki, grafana, otel-collector, promtail, alertmanager = lots of images to pull), I'll set `SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING=false`. This:
- Uses compose.yaml + compose.override.yaml only (no monitoring.yaml) → fewer images
- Skips the OTEL collector smoke check
- Skips the otel-collector health in smoke

This is cleaner for my resource-limited environment. And it's a documented toggle (`SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING=false`).

Wait, but does SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING affect the `up` compose args? Yes: `getComposeArgs = (env) => env.SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING === 'false' ? composeBaseArgs : composeWithMonitoringArgs`. So with SVA_ENABLE_MONITORING=false, up uses base+override only. Good.

But even base+override includes app(scaled 0), provisioner, migrate, bootstrap, candidate(0), redis, postgres. So provisioner/migrate/bootstrap would still start and build the image. Argh.

OK so the image build issue remains even without monitoring. Let me just check: does `up --scale app=0` actually build & start provisioner/migrate/bootstrap? Let me verify with `docker compose config` and by actually checking the behavior. Let me first list the services and see if there's any way these one-shots are excluded.

Let me run `docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.override.yaml config --services` to see.

Actually, you know what, let me just test the behavior directly but carefully. Let me first set up the vars, then run `pnpm env:up:local-builder` and observe. If it tries to build the image and that's too slow, I'll adapt by starting only postgres/redis.

Actually, a cleaner and much faster approach that stays faithful: I'll start the infra with an explicit service subset. The local profile's app is a dev server; the only infra it truly needs is postgres + redis. So:

`docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.override.yaml up -d postgres redis`

This starts just postgres and redis (no image build for app/provisioner/migrate/bootstrap since we only ask for postgres+redis which are plain images `postgres:16-alpine` and `redis:7-alpine`). Then I run migrations + bootstrap-app-user via nx, then start the dev server, then smoke/doctor.

But the canonical command is `env:up:local-builder`. To be faithful AND pragmatic, let me do this:
1. First, TRY the canonical `pnpm env:up:local-builder`. Observe if it builds the image (slow) or just starts infra.

Actually, let me reconsider — I bet the compose.yaml with override, when you `up` only a subset, is what a careful operator would do. But the canonical `up` starts everything. 

Let me just check what services `up --scale app=0` resolves and whether it builds. Let me run `docker compose ... config` to see the effective config, particularly the provisioner/migrate/bootstrap build settings. If they have `build: .`, `up` will build. Let me verify quickly.

Let me run a dry inspection.
